findings.title: Pagination off-by-one shows a blank last page
findings.body: totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which is wrong when user_count is an exact multiple of limit. With 100 members and limit 50, totalPages = 3 even though there are only 2 pages. Worse, the next() action (line 33) clamps offset to Math.min(offset + limit, user_count), so from page 2 it sets offset = 100, and findMembers requests offset=100 which returns an empty member list. The admin ends up on a blank page 3/3 for a group whose members all fit on two pages. The clamp and the totalPages formula need to use Math.ceil and clamp to user_count - limit.

findings.title: Group create action silently drops alias_level
findings.body: The JavaScript model's asJSON() (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js line 62) sends name, alias_level and visible, but the create action only reads params[:name] and params[:visible]. If an admin picks an alias level (e.g. 'everyone') in the new-group form, the group is created with alias_level 0 and the selection is silently lost. The update action (line 37) does honor params[:alias_level], so the two actions are inconsistent.

findings.title: Remove-member link rendered for automatic groups
findings.body: The template gates the remove link on {{#unless automatic}}, but this partial is rendered by the group-member item view whose context is the individual member (a Discourse.User), not the group. The member user object has no 'automatic' property, so the guard is always truthy-negative and the remove link is shown for automatic groups too (where the parent group.hbs template deliberately hides the add-members UI for automatic groups). Clicking it triggers removeMember on an automatic group, which the server rejects with a 422 and no user-visible error handling. The view should receive the group's automatic flag explicitly (e.g. via a computed property on the view or controller).

findings.title: add_members returns success even when no users matched
findings.body: add_members splits the username list and skips any username that doesn't match a user (the `if user = User.find_by_username(username)` guard), then unconditionally renders success_json. An admin who typos a username in the add-members box gets a success response and a member list refresh that doesn't contain the user, with no indication anything failed. The action should report which usernames could not be added (render_json_error) so the UI can surface it.

findings.title: Public members endpoint allows unbounded limit
findings.body: The members action takes `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` with no upper bound, on a route reachable by any logged-in (and possibly anonymous, subject to visibility) user. Passing limit=1000000 makes the server serialize up to a million member records in one response. The previous code capped the practical default at 200 for automatic groups; the new code should clamp limit to a sane maximum (e.g. 1000) before using it in the query.

findings.title: remove_member automatic-group spec uses wrong HTTP verb
findings.body: The test 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the route defined in config/routes.rb is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. Controller specs bypass routing so the test passes, but it does not exercise the actual DELETE route. Additionally, there is no request/routing spec at all for the new `put/delete /admin/groups/members` endpoints, so a routing regression would go unnoticed. The spec should use xhr :delete.
